description: Dead-man for the frame-differencing visual monitor (sensor.camera_visual_activity). Added 2026-08-30. Until now this was the ONLY monitor of the four with no dead-man, no derived binary_sensor and no availability guard - grep for camera_visual_activity across all 35 automations returned zero. That mattered because its most likely failure is not a crash but going BLIND while still running: cam_vision.py rewrites its state file every cycle regardless, and cam_motion.py used that file's mtime as its only freshness gate, so a camera nobody could actually see read as a camera that was quiet - the reassuring branch. The one signal that might have caught the monitor stopping (cam_flap's probe_shortfall) was calibrated for a single prober while two sensors probe the same endpoints, so cam_vision dying merely halved the probe stream to a level still above the bar. Fires on death OR on any camera going unseen for 15+ min; re-asserts hourly (:29) as a restart-wipe guard.

data.title: 📷 Camera vision monitor degraded
data.message: The frame-differencing visual monitor has been degraded for 30+ min (state: {{ states('sensor.camera_visual_activity') }}). While it is down, every per-camera staleness verdict falls back to "no verdict" rather than silently reading as a quiet area - that guard is deliberate. Summary: {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_visual_activity','summary') or 'attributes wiped' }}. Cameras not seen: {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_visual_activity','blind') or 'n/a' }}. Cross-camera corroboration in cam_motion.py is unaffected and still works. {{ now().strftime('%b %-d %-I:%M %p') }}.
